result.markdown: --- title: "Surrogate and emulator models" course-unit: a07-surrogate-models status: complete --- ## Why emulate a simulator? - An ODE solve can be accurate but too expensive inside calibration, uncertainty analysis, or design. - A surrogate approximates a declared simulator response on a declared domain. - The mechanistic model remains the arbiter for decisions. ::: {.notes} Emphasize that a surrogate is a computational approximation, not a new causal model. The held-out error plot is more important than the training fit. ::: ## A small, explicit target Classification: deterministic, continuous-time, continuous-state, population-level. $$ \dot S=-\beta cSI/N,\quad \dot I=\beta cSI/N-\gamma I,\quad \dot R=\gamma I. $$ For $\beta\in[0.02,0.08]$, emulate $$ q(\beta)=R(40;\beta)/N,\qquad e_j=\widehat q(\beta_j)-q(\beta_j). $$ Baseline: $(S,I,R)=(990,10,0)$, $N=1000$, $c=10$, $\gamma=0.25$. ## Design, simulate, fit ::: {#2 .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (::Surrogates.RadialBasis{Surrogates.var"#cubicRadial##0#cubicRadial##1", Int64, Vector{Float64}, Vector{Float64}, Float64, Float64, LinearAlgebra.Transpose{Float64, Vector{Float64}}, Float64, Bool, Float64}) (generic function with 1 method) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.notes} The Latin-hypercube design is deliberately small so the approximation error is visible and the example remains quick in CI. `RadialBasis` is callable in Surrogates.jl 7; `cubicRadial()` is the current constructor form. ::: ## The diagnostic is out of sample ::: {#4 .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html} ``` Mechanistic SIR output, radial-basis surrogate, training design, and held-out approximation error. ::: ::: $$ \operatorname{RMSE}=\sqrt{m^{-1}\sum_j e_j^2}. $$ ## Validate, then use - Check the emulator on held-out inputs, not only training points. - Refine locally with `Surrogates.update!` when error identifies a gap. - For two or more inputs, scale the design and increase training points. - Re-simulate every policy or scientific conclusion with the original model. ::: {#6 .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (rmse = 0.005079064991333957, max_abs_error = 0.030386676263557774) ``` ::: ::: ## Limits and links - Extrapolation outside the design interval is not validated. - A peak or threshold target can need many more points than a smooth final size. - Solver failures and observation noise must be represented in the training pipeline rather than hidden in one scalar response. See the [book appendix](../../appendices/07-surrogate-models.html), the [Surrogates radial-basis docs](https://docs.sciml.ai/Surrogates/stable/radials/), and the [surrogate interface](https://docs.sciml.ai/Surrogates/stable/surrogate/). ::: {.notes} Takeaway: design, fit, validate, and retain the simulator. A low RMSE is a local statement about this target, domain, and numerical implementation. :::
